summary: Galatea is a Nereid nymph, daughter of Nereus and Doris. In Ovid's Metamorphoses she loved the Sicilian river-god Acis; when the Cyclops Polyphemus killed him, she transformed Acis into the river that bears his name. She is distinct from Galatea, the name later applied to Pygmalion's statue.

sections.heading: Mythology
paragraphs: Hesiod, Homer, and Apollodorus name Galatea among the Nereids. Ovid gives her a speaking role in the love-triangle with Acis and Polyphemus on Sicily.
The Pygmalion statue named Galatea belongs to a separate Roman tradition and is not identified with this Nereid in the ancient Greek sources used here.
